title: Chapter 2 — The Weight of the Share

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER 2

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Weight of the Share
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They left the tomb at dusk.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The desert wind had already begun erasing their tracks. Sand slid into the open stairway behind them in soft continuous sheets, as if the ground itself preferred the hole filled. BAH-lahg walked ahead with the two remaining donkeys, spear across his shoulders. En-HEH-doo kept to the side, knife loose in her hand, eyes on the darkening ridges. Zeek brought up the rear, the journal and the compass both heavy against his ribs.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No one spoke for the first hour.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The donkeys noticed before any of them admitted it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The lead animal slowed every few hundred paces, ears twitching as though waiting for the familiar whistle that always came from somewhere behind the line. KOO-rash had been the one to soothe them when they grew stubborn. He talked to them more than he talked to people, inventing long stories they could not possibly understand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Now the lead donkey stopped altogether.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg sighed through his nose and walked back.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Come on.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The animal planted its feet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg tugged the lead rope.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Nothing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo watched for a moment.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: It keeps looking behind us.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: It smells him.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She shook her head.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: It smells that he's gone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg gave the donkey another patient pull.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I liked you better when you only corrected my archaeology.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I've never corrected your archaeology.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You've corrected everything else.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That earned the faintest curl at the corner of her mouth.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The expression vanished almost immediately.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg rested his forehead briefly against the donkey's neck before trying again.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Stubborn beast.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It learned from KOO-rash,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek said quietly.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The words surprised even him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked over his shoulder.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: So it did.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This time the donkey started walking without another protest.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For several minutes only the sound of hooves disturbed the desert.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Finally En-HEH-doo spoke.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: My brother used to whistle.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Neither man answered.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: He couldn't carry a tune to save his life.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Her eyes remained on the horizon.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: My mother always knew he was home because every dog in the neighborhood started barking.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Another stretch of silence.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: He died before he turned twenty.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg glanced sideways.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You've never mentioned him.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: There hasn't been a reason.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: And now?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She shrugged.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: There still isn't.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: But KOO-rash reminded you.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She considered lying.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Instead she nodded once.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: He reminded me that people disappear faster than habits do.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No one had an answer for that.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The wind shifted.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind them, another ribbon of sand spilled over the ridge where the tomb lay buried once more.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: KOO-rash's absence sat between them like a fourth set of footprints that refused to fade. Every gust left fewer places where KOO-rash had ever walked.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: When they finally stopped, BAH-lahg dropped his gear and began checking the animals' hooves with the same methodical care he gave every practical task. En-HEH-doo crouched a short distance away and cleaned dried blood from under her nails with the tip of her knife. The motion was precise, almost delicate.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek sat with his back against a low outcrop and stared at the linen wrapping on his left hand. The mark beneath it was quiet for the first time since the tomb. He did not trust the quiet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg finished with the donkeys and came to sit across from him. The big man did not look at the journal.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You counting the share already?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg asked.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek glanced up.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: KOO-rash's share. You're sitting there doing the arithmetic in your head. I've seen that face before.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek almost denied it. Then he shrugged.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: If I don't, somebody else will.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The words came out harder than he meant. He heard how cold they sounded and hated himself for a second.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg just grunted.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Someone always does. Doesn't mean I have to like watching it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He was quiet for a few breaths, then added, almost to the sand,
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: First crew I worked on, we lost a boy before we even reached the quarry. Fifteen years old. Same hungry look. Same fucking math.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He shook his head once.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Still don't like the sound of it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo's knife paused.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: He would have done the same to any of us if the numbers came out that way.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at her.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: That supposed to make it easier?

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: No. It's supposed to make it true.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They sat with that for a time. The desert cooled around them. Somewhere far off a night bird called once and did not call again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg eventually stood and checked the straps on the packs a second time, even though nothing had shifted. Zeek recognized the habit. The big man trusted his hands more than he trusted silence.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: We'll reach the city in two days if the weather holds,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Collector's going to notice the missing man.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Let him notice,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek answered.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo wiped the last of the blood from her blade and slid it home.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: He'll notice the extra silver more.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek almost smiled. Almost.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He opened the journal instead.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The last page was still waiting. The three lines in his father's hand had not changed. The ink no longer looked wet, but the paper itself felt slightly warmer than the desert night should have allowed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He closed it again before anything new could appear.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They slept in shifts. Zeek took the middle watch. He spent it staring at the dark and listening for the low vibration they had heard beneath the tomb. It did not come. The mark on his palm stayed quiet. The compass, when he checked it, still pointed straight down.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Toward morning En-HEH-doo relieved him. She sat without speaking for a long time, turning a small copper figurine between her fingers the way other people turned prayer tokens. Time had polished its smiling face nearly smooth.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You going to tell the Collector everything?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she asked eventually.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Good.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She tossed the figurine once and caught it.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Everything has a price. Some prices are better left unpaid.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek did not answer. He lay down, pulled his cloak over his face, and tried not to dream of water that wrote.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They broke camp at first light and continued toward Uruk.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind them, the last trace of KOO-rash's footprints disappeared under the morning wind.
